chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a mouse that falls into ghee (clarified butter) and oil, then is taken out from it alive, so he said, 'There is no harm in eating it.'
And regarding a mouse that dies in ghee and honey, he said, 'Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'Take what is around it and eat the remainder.'
And regarding a mouse that dies in oil, he said, 'Do not eat it, but use it to grease your saddle.'

key_terms.أَسْرِجْ بِهِ: Use it for greasing a saddle (leather)
key_terms.الزَّيْت: Oil (specifically olive oil or similar liquid fat)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating ghee or oil if a mouse falls into it alive or dies inside it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *istihlak* (dilution/consumption), where the small impurity is considered nullified by the large volume of the medium. It highlights a practical distinction in classical fiqh: while ghee and honey allow for the removal of the immediate vicinity, oil requires complete disposal or repurposing (such as greasing leather) due to its different absorption properties. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on ease and the removal of hardship in daily consumption matters.
